conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You’re here because of abdominal pain and fevers that came back after your last discharge. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. I felt okay the day I got home, but the next day, the pain came back—sharp, in my upper belly, shooting to my back. I took my Dilaudid, but it didn’t help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And then what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I woke up with a fever—102.3. Took Tylenol, it went down. Then I started vomiting—green stuff, not bloody. Felt so weak after, I almost passed out in the bathroom.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You mentioned you didn’t fully lose consciousness—you could still hear the TV?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right. I felt the curtain closing in, slumped down, but I was aware. After about 20 seconds, I opened my eyes and got up slowly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds scary. Given your POTS, this could be related to a drop in blood pressure when you stood up. We’ll keep an eye on that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I’ve had that before. But the pain and fever—could it be pancreatitis again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. Your lipase is normal, which is surprising, but with your history, we’re treating this like a flare. We’ll keep you NPO for now—no food by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ve done that before. Will I get IV fluids?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve already started two liters of normal saline. You were dehydrated. We’ll continue that and give you IV Dilaudid for pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. And my methotrexate? I was supposed to get it this week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you your 25mg dose by injection while you’re here. Your rheumatologist wants to keep you on it—it’s been helping your vasculitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve noticed my digestion has been better since starting it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are stable—no infection in blood or urine. We did an ultrasound yesterday—gallbladder looks fine, no stones.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Was the pancreas clear?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s hard to see due to bowel gas, but there’s no fluid around it, which is reassuring. We didn’t do a CT because your exam hasn’t changed much from past scans.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’d rather avoid another CT if we can. So what now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you on IV fluids and pain meds. If your pain improves, we’ll start you on clear liquids tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing better. Pain is down, and you haven’t vomited since yesterday. We’re going to try clear liquids—apple juice, broth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Can I have ginger ale?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, as long as it’s flat. We’ll watch for nausea. Also, we restarted your amitriptyline and escitalopram this morning—they were held while you were NPO.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been feeling anxious. Glad to have those back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You tolerated the clear liquids well. We’re advancing you to full liquids—yogurt, pudding, cream of wheat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I have mashed potatoes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Soon. Let’s stick to smooth foods for now. We want to avoid stressing your pancreas.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Urine culture came back—no significant growth. So no UTI. That’s good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the rash I had in the ER? It’s gone now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Likely related to your vasculitis or a viral reaction. Since it’s resolved and no other signs, we’re not worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t had a bowel movement in days. Is that normal?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, and with your opioid use, constipation is a concern. We’ll keep you on docusate and senna.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. Pain is mild, you’re eating soft foods, and you’re more mobile. We’re going to switch you to oral pain meds—Dilaudid by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’d prefer that. IVs are uncomfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today we’re planning your discharge for tomorrow. You’re tolerating a bland diet, pain is controlled, and you’re walking without dizziness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What about my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re increasing your escitalopram to 20mg at night for anxiety. Pantoprazole will be twice daily to protect your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And betaxolol?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re increasing it to 20mg daily for POTS. You’ll get a prescription for that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been using midodrine at home, but it gives me headaches lying down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s why we didn’t restart it here. Fludrocortisone and betaxolol should help enough.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I be worried if the fever comes back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Also watch for worsening pain, vomiting, or dizziness. If any of those happen, come back right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my weight loss—15 pounds. Should I see a dietitian?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good idea. We’ll refer you. Your malabsorption has improved, but nutrition is key with chronic pancreatitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home today. You’re stable, walking, and eating well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll follow up with rheumatology and GI?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and your primary doctor too. Keep taking your enzymes with meals—they help digestion.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t forget. And I’ll get my methotrexate injection on schedule.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll send all prescriptions to your pharmacy. Take it easy at home, and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Get some rest and stay hydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try. The fatigue has been real.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s been a tough few days. Give yourself time to recover.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And I’ll avoid heavy meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Smart. Stick to small, low-fat meals. Your pancreas will thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. No fried food, no big portions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. And keep up with your bowel regimen—don’t let constipation sneak up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll take my senna every morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good plan. We’ll see you in follow-up soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you again, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will bring your discharge papers shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll wait for them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care of yourself.
